references.text: Here the creation by God's word is mentioned, which can be seen as parallel to how Jesus, by the power of the Holy Spirit, becomes conceived.
The reference to 'Immanuel', meaning 'God with us', points forward to the incarnation of Jesus, who is God's Son.
David's Lord is mentioned, pointing forward to the Messiah, God's Son, who is higher than kings.
The prophecy of a righteous branch, which is a reference to the Messiah, who will be called the Lord our righteousness.
The angel's message to Mary that she will become pregnant by the Holy Spirit and give birth to a son, who will be called God's Son.
Jesus, who is greater than the angels, and who has inherited a more excellent name than they, as God's Son.
